admiration.description: Respect or appreciation for someone or something regarded as impressive, skilled, or excellent; distinguish from simply agreeing with an opinion (approval).

amusement.description: Finding something funny or entertaining, often with laughter; distinguish from general happiness (joy).

anger.description: Strong displeasure or hostility about a perceived wrong or obstacle; distinguish from milder irritation (annoyance) and a negative judgment without anger (disapproval).

annoyance.description: Mild irritation or frustration at something bothersome; distinguish from stronger anger.

approval.description: Agreement, acceptance, or a favorable opinion; distinguish from admiration of excellence and affection (love).

caring.description: Concern, sympathy, or a wish to support another person and protect their wellbeing; distinguish from gratitude for help received.

confusion.description: Not understanding something or being unable to make sense of it; distinguish from an interested search for information (curiosity).

curiosity.description: Interest in learning, exploring, or knowing more; a question alone does not establish curiosity, and lack of understanding may instead express confusion.

desire.description: A strong wish or longing for something; wanting an outcome does not by itself imply expecting it to happen (optimism).

disappointment.description: Unhappiness because hopes or expectations were not met; distinguish from general sadness without an unmet expectation.

disapproval.description: Disagreement, criticism, or a negative opinion about something; distinguish from the emotional intensity of anger and the revulsion of disgust.

disgust.description: Revulsion or strong aversion to something offensive, repulsive, or unpleasant, physically or morally; distinguish from simple disagreement.

embarrassment.description: Self-conscious discomfort, awkwardness, or shame about exposure or how one is seen; distinguish from remorse about an action one regrets.

excitement.description: High-energy enthusiasm or eagerness about something happening or anticipated; distinguish from calmer happiness (joy) and a wish alone (desire).

fear.description: Being scared or sensing danger or a threat; distinguish from uneasy anticipation or nervous tension (nervousness).

gratitude.description: Thankfulness or appreciation for help, kindness, or a benefit received; distinguish from admiration of a quality or achievement.

grief.description: Deep sorrow, especially in response to death or significant loss; distinguish from more general sadness.

joy.description: Happiness, pleasure, or delight; distinguish from finding something funny (amusement) and high-energy enthusiasm (excitement).

love.description: Affection, attachment, or strong fondness for a person, activity, or thing; distinguish from agreement (approval) and concern for wellbeing (caring).

nervousness.description: Anxiety, worry, or uneasy tension about something uncertain or anticipated; distinguish from being directly frightened by a threat (fear).

optimism.description: Hope or confidence that things may turn out well; distinguish from merely wanting a particular outcome (desire).

pride.description: Satisfaction or esteem in oneself, an achievement, or someone or a group one identifies with; distinguish from admiration without this personal connection.

realization.description: Coming to understand, notice, or discover something; distinguish from remaining confused and from surprise at an unexpected event.

relief.description: Reassurance or relaxation when worry, distress, or an unwanted situation eases; distinguish from happiness without a preceding burden.

remorse.description: Regret, guilt, or an apology about something done or left undone; distinguish from embarrassment about social exposure and caring for someone else.

sadness.description: Unhappiness, sorrow, or feeling down; distinguish from disappointment tied to an unmet expectation and deep loss-focused grief.

surprise.description: A reaction to something unexpected or astonishing, whether pleasant or unpleasant; distinguish from simply coming to understand something (realization).

neutral.description: No clearly expressed emotion from the other GoEmotions categories, or a neutral reaction; includes factual statements and task requests. This is not a recognition-error or uncertainty label.
